name: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina
history: A Capuchin friar who for fifty years bore the wounds of Christ in his hands, feet and side. From the friary of San Giovanni Rotondo in southern Italy he heard confessions for many hours a day, drew pilgrims from all over the world, and founded a great hospital for the relief of suffering. He was canonised in 2002.
life: Francesco Forgione was born at Pietrelcina, near Benevento, in 1887, the son of farmers. He entered the Capuchin novitiate at fifteen, taking the name Pio, and was ordained in 1910. Poor health kept him at home for long periods, and in 1916 he was sent to San Giovanni Rotondo, where he spent the rest of his life. On 20 September 1918, praying before a crucifix, he received the visible stigmata. The wounds were examined by doctors and by the Holy See, and in the early 1930s, while the case was investigated, he was forbidden for a time to say Mass in public or to hear confessions. He obeyed. Crowds came to his Mass and to his confessional, where he could be gentle or severe. He encouraged prayer groups and built the hospital Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, opened in 1956. He died on 23 September 1968.
prayerTo: Saint Pio, you shared the wounds of Christ and spent your days reconciling sinners to God. Pray for all who are sick and all who care for them, for priests in the confessional, and for me, that I may make a good confession, carry my cross without complaint, and learn to pray, hope and not worry. Amen.
penance: Go to confession this week if you can, and pray the Rosary today for someone who is ill.
meditation: Pray, hope and don’t worry, he told those who came to him. Which worry could you hand over to God in prayer today?
